strengths: Strong empirical results with 3-10 dB PSNR improvements and ~50% reduction in perceptual error (LPIPS) over baselines on two established benchmarks
Clear problem formulation: identifies genuine limitation of time-conditioned models failing at out-of-distribution extrapolation, with practical applications
Technically sound approach combining Deformable 3D Gaussians with Latent ODEs in a sensible two-stage framework; variational formulation properly handles stochasticity
Elegant lightweight solution: second-derivative regularization (Eq. 5) effectively prevents unphysical high-frequency oscillations without computational overhead
Comprehensive evaluation across 17 diverse scenes from two datasets with multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) and both quantitative and qualitative results
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (Deformable 3D Gaussians [38] for Stage 1, Latent ODEs [32] for Stage 2) without substantial methodological innovation
Critical missing ablation: no justification or comparison for the freezing strategy in Stage 1. Why freeze rather than jointly train? Is this design choice necessary or merely convenient?

Incomplete ablations on key design choices: no sensitivity analysis for regularizer weight λ_reg, limited V-ODE vs D-ODE comparison despite marginal differences in several scenes, and missing curriculum learning details (referenced as 'Section ??')

Evaluation limited to synthetic and controlled scenes (D-NeRF fully synthetic; NVFI controlled captures): no real-world video evaluation, complex occlusions, or long-term extrapolation analysis (how far beyond training window?)
Computational cost analysis entirely missing: no runtime, memory, or training time comparisons with baselines despite ODE solving adding computational overhead
Presentation not fully finalized: problem definition duplicated, incomplete section reference ('Section ??'), suggesting manuscript not ready for publication
No latent space analysis: missing visualization or interpretation of learned latent dynamics; unclear if model captures meaningful motion patterns or merely fits trajectories
Limited failure case analysis: no discussion of motion types that break the method (chaotic, discontinuous, highly stochastic), and performance drops on 'Trex' and 'Bouncingballs' unexplained

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation: The paper addresses dynamic scene extrapolation (beyond observed time), an important but under-explored problem distinct from interpolation.
Principled technical approach: Using latent ODEs to enforce spatio-temporal smoothness is well-justified; avoids timestamp conditioning via sequence-to-sequence formulation.
Strong empirical results: Consistent state-of-the-art performance across three benchmarks (D-NeRF, NVFi, HyperNeRF) with substantial improvements (18-40%) over GaussianPrediction baseline.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Thorough ablations (Tables 4, 6, 7) demonstrating value of each component (ODE, regularization, adaptive weighting, dynamic sampling); both quantitative and qualitative results.

Thoughtful design choices: Dynamic trajectory sampling for varying prediction horizons, adaptive regularization weighting to avoid early-training collapse, and clean separation of interpolation/forecasting stages.

Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Clear writing, informative visualizations (especially Figure 2), detailed appendix with architecture, hyperparameters, and implementation details enabling reproduction.
weaknesses: Limited component-level novelty: Individual pieces (canonical+deformation, latent ODEs, Transformers) are from prior work; contribution is primarily in their combination for 3DGS extrapolation rather than methodological innovation.

Severe practical limitations - per-scene training requirement: Each scene requires separate optimization; multi-scene training (Table 8) shows 3-10 dB PSNR degradation, severely limiting real-world applicability.
Inadequate analysis of extrapolation horizons: Only 20-25% future windows tested; no systematic study of performance degradation with longer horizons or maximum reliable extrapolation distance.
Fundamental limitation with abrupt motion: Method fails on scenes with discontinuities (bouncingballs, trex); smoothness prior cannot handle non-smooth dynamics. No proposed mitigation strategy.

Critical dependency on interpolation quality: Extrapolation inherits all interpolation errors without analysis of error propagation; fallingball example shows interpolation failure → extrapolation failure.

Incomplete ablations and sensitivity analysis: Limited justification for design choices (why Tanh activations? why λ_latent=10^-5 vs λ_traj=10^-1?); hyperparameter Tc varies per-dataset without guidance; no computational cost comparisons.
Weaker real-world performance: HyperNeRF results significantly smaller than synthetic datasets; keyboard scene shows minimal improvement, questioning cross-domain generalization.
Missing evaluation of temporal coherence: Standard metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) may not capture temporal smoothness quality; no user studies or motion-specific metrics.

strengths: Clear problem formulation distinguishing extrapolation from interpolation with principled motivation for using ODEs to enforce smoothness
Clever decoupling of scene reconstruction from temporal forecasting that elegantly avoids timestamp conditioning and OOD failures
Significant empirical improvements: 20-40% gains over baselines across D-NeRF, NVFi, and HyperNeRF benchmarks
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablations demonstrating the necessity of each component
Sound technical design including adaptive regularization weighting and dynamic trajectory sampling strategy
Strong presentation quality with clear pipeline illustration and detailed appendices supporting reproducibility
Convincing ablations showing autoregressive baseline doubles LPIPS error, validating the continuous latent ODE formulation
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: latent ODEs and Transformers are established; main contribution is their combination with 3DGS
Strong dependency on interpolation model quality with no graceful failure handling; errors propagate directly to extrapolation
Fundamentally cannot handle scenes with discontinuous or abrupt motion changes due to smoothness assumptions
Multi-scene generalization significantly underperforms single-scene training, limiting practical applicability as general-purpose model
Deterministic formulation sacrifices uncertainty quantification important for safety-critical applications; variational variant substantially underperforms
Extrapolation evaluated only within 20-25% of training horizon; no analysis of degradation for longer extrapolation or effective limits
Extensive dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning may hinder reproducibility and generalization
Computational costs not addressed; no timing comparisons for two-stage training or inference speed analysis
Limited analysis of failure modes and no mechanism to assess reliability or predict when extrapolation will succeed
Design choices (L1 loss, Tc=30, ODE solver selection) lack sufficient justification or sensitivity analysis
